Deadhouse Gates starts out with a whole new cast of characters on an entirely different continent called Seven Cities. Is
Erikson a sadist and just likes to be difficult?
Yes.

But also, Memories of Ice was originally supposed to be the second book of the series. About 180 pages into writing the book his computer died and lost all of his work. Damn. Considering he had Gardens of the Moon written in 1992, locked in a 10 book deal, published Gardens in 1999, and needed to finish a full length novel that supposed to follow up
a book he wrote almost 7-8 years ago. Rather than go through to write it from the beginning, he decided to work on
Deadhouse Gates which he realizes is the right choice for the series in the long run.
Gardens of the Moon
Prologue: Unta, capital of the Malazan Empire
Deadhouse Gates
1163rd Year of Burn’s Sleep, takes place after Gardens of the Moon
Unta, Capital city of the Malazan Empire
The Season of Rot
Nobles arrested at midnight, dragged from their beds into mock trials with juries of beggars
A ceremony in Unta performed by priests of Hood where they strip naked, smear themselves with blood of executed murderers to attract flies (sprites of Hood) and walk through the streets
This is the third ceremony in ten years, unprecedented frequency (Laseen has ruled for nine)
Three characters stand in chains among other criminals and nobles culled, waiting to be paraded through mobs of peasants to the slave ships
Felisin Paran: youngest Paran sibling
Heboric Light Touch: ex-thief, priest of Fener (Boar god of war) & historian who wrote a “treasonous” history that accused Empress Laseen of murder and “bungled the job”
Both hands cut off long ago
Fellow historian Duiker spoke words in his defense at his trial
Baudin: a large thug
A priest approaches and speaks Felisin and Heboric, and then dissipates to reveal no-one underneath
Tavore Paran is the new Adjunct after Lorn
Renounced her House and her nobleborn status
Ganoes has “disappeared” on Genabackis, he's suspected of treason, their parents confirmed dead
Felisin believes Tavore did this all to show Tavore’s loyalty to the Empress
Tavore appears, watching over the procession with her personal, mysterious aide T’amber and a company of Red Blades (called Red Swords here)
Red, magic-resistant otataral links woven in their chainmail
The Empress gains adoration and support from the poor lower class
Carefully triggered riots, controlled looting and slaughter to satisfy the mobs’ bloodlust, and reimpose order
All against the “treasonous, scheming” noble class
The seized assets provided the Empress the resources to pay the Empire’s  martial expansions
The prisoners are dragged through the streets with lines of soldiers holding back the peasants as the mob throw rocks, bricks, and fists
No one dares touch the priest
Baudin kills anybody who touches him
A breach in the line of the soldiers opens and the mobs flood the prisoners, beating everyone bloody including Heboric
Baudin, in attempt to appease the mob, grabs a noble (Lady Gaesan), snapped her neck, and sawed her head off with his chains
Everyone freezes as they watch Baudin decapitate the noblewoman
Soldiers and Red Blades come to disperse the mob
Of the three hundred at the start of the march, less than a hundred reached the slave ships
The farmers and peasants look upon them with sorrow instead of the violence and frenzy their city counterparts had shown

Seven Cities is a continent that was founded by the seven original Holy Cities, each ruled by a Holy Protector (priest-ruler) called a Holy Falah’d. There are other Holy Cities, but they don’t have a Holy Falah’d.
Pan’potsun Odhan
1164 Burn’s Sleep, the story moves into the next year
Bestest boy Mappo Runt, full blooded Trell, and Icarium, half-blooded Jaghut
Icarium had failed to disguise himself as a Tanno [tribe] Spiritwalker [priest/elder] in the Holy City, Ehrlitan
They observe an aptorian demon in the distance, possibly a scout for Shadowthrone but may be possessed by Sha’ik
They believe their next water hole has Sha’ik’s army camped around it
Icarium oils his hornwood longbow and his one-edged longsword
Mappo (reluctantly) and Icarium descend into the desert basin
The duo come across one of many ruins of long dead civilizations across the Pan’potsun Odhan and the Holy Desert
“From the Holy Desert emerged the legend of Dryjhna the Apocalyptic”
Near the courtyard center they find a six feet high pink marble column
At the foot they note claw marks and guess it is rats, possibly the D’ivers form of someone named Gryllen
Soletaken is the ability to shapeshift into another animal form, D’ivers shapeshifts into multiples of the same animal
Gryllen may be one of many other Soletaken/D’ivers seeking rumoured mythical gates that offer Ascendancy
Icarium laments about his missing memories and seeks this “convergence” in hopes of learning more about himself (his character’s ultimate goal), much to Mappo’s apprehension
Trivia: a tel is a city mound or hill made when a city falls, the residents knock all the walls down and rebuild on top of the rubble, denoted by the suffix -mon
The duo are approached by Ryllandaras in his D’ivers form of six wolves
‘The spicy scent of D’ivers filled the night air’
Ryllandaras speaks inside their minds
We learn from Mappo that Ryllandaras is the brother of Treach (Tiger god of war), that Treach killed him somewhere on Quon Tali, and that Ryllandaras was D’ivers jackals then
Ryllandaras thought about attacking them but backs the fuck off when he realizes they are Mappo Runt and Icarium
Mappo is thankful; “Before you unleash all that I am sworn to prevent”
Ryllandaras goes back to hunting the demon of Shadow (aptorian)
Mappo sternly warns that the demon belongs to Sha’ik or the Holy Desert, who Ryllandaras doesn't recognize and doesn't care
Ryllandaras walks off into a gloom of sorcery
Hissar, Imperial Harbour
Duiker, Imperial Historian
Thanks to “Ten Very Big Books” interview with Steven Erikson himself, it’s actually pronounced “dooker” which was how I pronounced it in my head the first time I am vindicated
Mallick Rel, chief advisor to High Fist Pormqual who commands the Malazan armies on the Seven Cities continent
Is a Jhistal (uses blood for ritual magic) priest of Mael (Elder God of the seas)
History lesson:
The Wickans are plains warriors from the Quon Tali continent
The Wickans are divided into clans and fought amongst each other until Coltaine united them to fight against the Malazan Empire
Clans: Crow, Foolish Dog, and Weasel
The Wickans had lost to the Malazan 7th Army, but Emperor Kellanved had managed to gain their loyalty to fight for the Empire
The 7th Army were then sent to Seven Cities where they conquered and made Hissar their HQ
After Kellanved died and Laseen usurped, she sent the Wickans to rot in backwater villages

When the Genabackan campaign failed and rebellion was starting in Seven Cities, Laseen was desperate for competent leaders so she gave Coltaine (who himself led a rebellion) command of the 7th Army to put down the Seven Cities rebellion
Duiker and Mallick Rel watch the Wickan soldiers disembark
Duiker distrusts Mallick Rel and is suspicious how quickly he rose through the ranks
Rumors in the army that Mallick Rel blackmailed High First Pormqual and has murdered those who got in his way
Malazan politics in Seven Cities is a mess
Duiker says he's here to see prisoners be shipped to the otataral mines
Red coloured, mysterious, magic-deadening ore
Mines usually reserved for mages, mages have died either by exposure or deprivation from their warrens. Currently unsure which
An unnamed captain and Kulp, the 7th Army’s lone surviving mage, arrives noting the brewing riot
Fighting is about to break out as bad blood rises between the Wickans and the Hissar Guard
Hissar Guard is pissed, being the same Malazan 7th Army that defeated them, only to have their former enemy Wickan be their commander
Coltaine stepped in with an ululating scream, sending the Wickans into an organized parade
Everyone is impressed
Fiddler, Kalam, Crokus, Apsalar (formerly Sorry), and Moby are on a boat
Arrived at imperial port Karakarang, spent a week in Rutu Jelba to get a ship, sailing the Kansu Sea, passed through the Skara Isles, headed to Ehrlitan
A dhenrabi Soletaken appears, spicy bitter scent reveals it's a Soletaken and taunts them telepathically
Fiddler shot an incendiary clay ball from his crossbow that detonated in the dhenrabi’s mouth, its head explodes
A drunk night in Rutu Jelba, Kalam reveals to Crokus that during the Seven Cities conquest, Whiskeyjack had marched his crew to chase Quick Ben across the Holy Desert Raraku with Kalam as their guide
Kalam and QB are Seven Cities natives that fought as a part of the Falah’dan against the Malazans, Kalam planned to betray the WJ
Crokus asks why they didn't just sail straight to Quon Tali if their purpose was to take Apsalar home to set things right
He guesses it was only an excuse to return to the Empire
wtf?
Fiddler and Kalam reveal that Kalam is going after Laseen
Apsalar pales and has a half-smile “that belonged to her when she had been someone else”
Apsalar “remembers” that Kalam was a Falah’dan Dagger, and the Malazan Claw gave him command of a Hand (squad of 5 assassins)
Quick Ben is their ‘shaved knuckle in the hole’
Real world history: knucklebones are the primitive form of dice, taken from the knucklebones of sheep, goat, or calf, and used since the ancient times of Greece
“Shaved” as in cheating, liked loaded dice
“In the hole” as in QB’s warren that can summon him at Kalam’s side in a heartbeat
They chose to start in Seven Cities because to continent is about to rise up in Rebellion, Quick Ben’s wild idea
Duiker walks in the rain through Hissar to the edge of the city
Sees an ochre handprint and ponders on the secret symbols the Malazans have ignored, possibly fatal with the Year of Dryjhna (Apocalypse) approaching
Walks into a tent at a trader encampment pretending to be Dosii (a native of Dosin Pali)
Buys food from a hawker (vendor) and gossips about the Mezlas (derogatory term for Malazans)
Watches two Semk tribe seers performed divination to communicate with the spirit of Dryjhna
They bring out a boy with gouged out eyes and potbelly, a suffering soul
‘Two fountains of raging blood! Face to face. The blood is the same, the two are the same and salty waves shall wash the shores of Raraku. The Holy Desert remembers its past!’
A human shape of fire forms in the space
The boy dies and the tribes fall weeping
A figure with a goat’s-head hood and black hides in the shadows
Duiker ponders of the ancient civilization of Seven Cities, built upon layers of layers of past older cities and the spirits that lay here
The Imperial Historian leaves the encampment and heads to the Imperial Compound to meet with the new Fist
Two guards stop him thinking him Dosii and remark that another came like him
At the council: Mallick Rel, Kulp, Coltaine, and Bult
Duiker notes his presence was unexpected by Mallick Rel and sees his discomfort
Duiker greets Coltaine who recounts how they met in battle
Duiker almost died by Bult’s lance
Dujek redirected Bult’s lance attack on Duiker and slashed his face
Bult’s horse crunched Dujek’s arm which led to its amputation and why he is now Dujek Onearm
Duiker had worn no weapons or armor in the Wickan Wars but takes precaution now that he’s older
The council waits on Coltaine’s warlocks
Empress Laseen in her first year had mass crucified all the Wickan warlocks
The Wickans were not worried, crows had come to collect their souls and wait for their reincarnation
A bow legged boy with a goat’s head hood enters revealed as Sormo E’nath
Sormo E’nath took 11 days to die, one crow came for each day to collect his soul
Duiker notes the Rhivi of Genabackis have similar beliefs in newborns being the vessel to hold souls
Sormo E’nath and Duiker talk about how they witnessed the divination together that promised armageddon (Rebellion)
Sormo notes Mallick Rel has hidden motives
Coltaine cares nothing of hidden motives or angry sentiments against him. As long as they obey, he will serve
Mallick Rel delivers High Fist Pormqual’s welcome to Coltaine as the new Fist of the 7th Army and new orders
He notes the 7th is one of the three original Malazan armies
Admiral Nok of the Malazan Navy is to leave Hissar to go to Aren
High Fist Coltaine is to march 400 leagues overland to Aren for Pormqual to test the 7th Army and its new troops
Bult says that’s stupid, both that the 400 league march just for Pormqual to sneer at them and that it would leave eastern Seven Cities unoccupied
400 leagues ≈ 1200 miles, or over the length from LA to Seattle
Bult also remarks that Mallick Rel isn’t apart of the High Command, Empress Laseen doesn’t even know who he is outside Pormqual’s reports to her
Bult calls Mallick Rel nothing but a messenger boy and kicks him out of the council
Duiker advises to Coltaine that may not have been wise
Coltaine doesn’t care, he was quite content
Coltaine asks what’s Pormqual like
Pormqual actually doesn’t do shit
Most edicts come from Mallick Rel and other noble-born merchants
Responsible for tax cuts on imports and tax raises on local goods and exports, of course exempting the merchants’ own personal exports
Pormqual had been High Fist for four years
Cartheron Crust, along with his brother Urko Crust, was the High Fist before Pormqual, drowned in Aren. Their bodies never found
Cartheron Crust, Urko Crust, Toc the Elder, and Ameron were Kellanved’s Old Guard who disappeared
Since Duiker witnessed Mallick’s humiliation, he’d be unworthy to spy on him and so Duiker is attached to Coltaine’s staff
The council ends, Duiker and Kulp leave and find a room to speak in private
Kulp distrusts Coltaine and is very nervous about Sormo E’nath
Duiker then asks Kulp to help free Heboric from the Otataral mines, just pick him up on the island’s coast
Trivia: They realize they are in Fist Torlom’s former office where a Dryjhnii assassin killed her
Fiddler disguised himself as a Gral tribesmen, known for vendettas so no one would mess with him and wanders the city as he waits for Kalam to contact his old agents in the city
Ehrlitan is a Holy City of marble built by the hill that used to be Jen’rahb, a city nine times bigger with temples and buildings rising in the shape of a Crown
The subterranean tunnels collapsed under the weight and the entire city had fallen
A kitchen helper, the lone survivor, believed he caused the collapse when he dropped a beaker and took his life on the paving stone that is presently commemorated to him
The Red Blades are slaughtering those they believe are allies of Dryjhna
In the chaos, Fiddler sees a simharal (child seller, pimp) pick up two girls and run into an alley
Fiddler goes into the alley and buys the girls from him
The older girl leads them home
Fiddler is met by guards who abandoned the girls when the Red Blades came, Captain Turqa comes and takes Fiddler to meet the girls’ grandfather
Kimloc, the Tanno Spiritwalker, is grateful and suspects immediately that Fiddler is a Malazan spy
Captain Turqa knows about the Bridgeburners being outlawed
Fiddler wants to leave soon, but the Rebellion has made it difficult to book passage on a boat so they’re forced to travel over land
Kimloc warns that Raraku will blow the whirlwind of the Apocalypse
Also of a coming convergence of soletaken and d’ivers
The Path of Hands draws shapeshifters by instinct, the victor rumoured to attain Ascendancy and dominate their own kind
Kimloc offers a Tanno song in exchange for the story of the Bridgeburners, a sorcery devoted to peace with the potential for Ascendency
Kimloc simply needs to touch Fiddler to learn his history, Fiddler firmly rejects
Kimloc presents Fiddler with a conch shell as a treasure

‘Raraku was once a sea. Such remnants can be found in the Holy Desert, provided you know the location of the ancient shores. In addition to the memory song contained within it, of that inland sea, other songs have been invested. My own songs of power.’
As Fiddler gets up to leave, Kimloc laid a hand on Fiddler’s shoulder
Captain Turqa reveals the last visitor Kimloc had was eleven years ago with Dujek Onearm to negotiate the surrender of Karakarang, the Holy City of the Tanno cult
Kimloc did not want his people to die after T’lan Imass had slaughtered the Holy City Aren
Fiddler tried to explain no one had given the Logros T’lan Imass (which Emperor Kellanved commanded) the order to attack, but Turqa didn’t want to hear it
Fiddler returns to the crew
Fiddler and Kalam notice all the symbols on the walls
The city will be uprising in about a week
They also note the unhuman handprints and guess its due to the convergence (Path of Hands)
Fiddler doesn’t tell Kalam about Kimloc
Fiddler knows he’ll go kill Kimloc, his family, and his guards (meta: unknown to book readers why)
Apsalar being out of sight makes Fiddler nervous
Still afraid of Cotillion, Patron of Assassins, taking back control and killing them all
Kalam goes to the Jen’rahb hill to meet his contact, Mebra
The Malazan patrol was thinly spread and easy to stealth past
Kalam looks back to the city and sees the Fist’s Keep
Ehrlitan’s paranoid, cowardly Fist (unnamed) holed himself up in his office, ignoring the Red Blades and spies
Unable to accommodate the soldiers called from all the garrisons around Ehrlitan and only a few soldiers held the Imperial Docks
The Malazans are mentally “under siege”
Kalam finds Mebra, a Seven Cities native spy for the Malazans
Kalam asks for the new signs and symbols to navigate safe passage through the Odhan
Mebra drops the Holy Book of Dryjhna stolen from High Fist Pormqual’s vaults in Aren
When the Book of Dryjhna is delivered to Sha’ik, leader of the Whirlwind, the Whirlwind will be raised from the Holy Desert Raraku and Rebellion will come
Kalam takes the Holy Book of Dryjhna to deliver to Sha’ik and ensure safe passage through the Odhan
If threatened Kalam will destroy the Book

Mebra’s instructions: ride a sand-coloured stallion, red telaba (cloak), each night unwrap the book and call upon Dryjhna to obliterate his trail, wait an hour in silence, and never expose the book to sunlight
Kalam leaves
The Red Blades appear, this was a planned set-up
Lostara Yil, a captain, follows Kalam’s trail
Tene Baralta, commander, holds a fragment of bhederin hide that’s part of the binding of the Holy Book he can use to track the Book through sorcery
Mebra convinces Tene to spare Kalam because he suspects Kalam will try to return to Malaz (and go after Laseen)
The duo were attacked by a dozen D’ivers leopards
One bites Mappo’s neck and Mappo kills it, Mappo is poisoned
Icarium goes berserk and kills four before Mappo finishes one and chased the ones that ran away
Icarium stabs an arrow in the ground to warn others who dare attack the duo
The duo reach a cliff that divides Raraku from the Panpot’sun Odhan
Inside the fissure in the cliff reveals a tower with only a window at the top
Messremb, a Soletaken bear, arrives and veers into human form
Human form is 5 feet tall and emaciated skinny
Greets his old friend Mappo, didn't know he travels with Icarium
Resumes his journey on the Path of Hands
Iskaral Pust arrives sitting cross legged on an ebon mule
High Priest of Shadow of Tesem Temple
Tesem Temple used to be for the Queen of Dreams until it was abandoned
Bhok’arala (monkey faced bats, Moby is one) nests in the temple
Servant appears with wine and pulls them up via a pulley rope system
Servant is very strong and his accent is Malazan
Mappo notes that a warren opened when the ebon mule ran into the temple
Icarium forgets all about the leopard battle, is aware of his memory loss, sees that they are both injured
Mappo lies and says he used Icarium’s weapons to fight off a leopard at night
Felisin has sex with Beneth, a Korelri slave that worked for Captain Sawark and is ‘king’ of Skullcup, so that Heboric can get more rest
Felisin learned that she could use sex to make arrangements to ensure Heboric, Baudin, and her survival and believes is the reason they're still alive
Assumed Capt. Sawark had orders to work Heboric to death
Thinks about Heboric’s otataral theory
Limestone is the bones of things once living
Otataral is like a layer of melted fat sandwiched between layers of limestone
The island melted via a big sorcery event which made the otataral veins
Felisin follows Beneth to Bula’s Inn
A gate guard, Pella, says the Dosii guards (natives) are becoming irresponsible and keep talking about the rebellion
He quotes Kellanved from Duiker’s ‘Imperial Campaigns: Volume One’ and tells Felisin it's worth learning what happens next after the quote
Sinker Lake is a possible escape route Felisin watches
Felisin comes home from Bula’s Inn after drinking wine, Heboric is pissed that Felisin is reduced to a whore
Heboric smells durhang (opiate, something like hashish) on her
Sinker Lake’s level dropped a hands length
Baudin comes home, she doesn't know what he does every night
Baudin and Heboric talk, Felisin feels pissed they exclude her despite what she does for their sake
She feels lonely and increasingly dependent on Beneth, his durhang, and his body to cope
Admiral Nok, the Malazan Sahul Fleet, and Mallick Rel have departed from Hissar to Aren for Pormqual’s recall
The harbor market is full of natives  excited that their occupiers have left
Duiker and Kulp stand at the harbor, Dosin Pali (lone city on the otataral mine island) can be seen across the ocean
Kulp informs that instructions has been sent to Heboric
Red Blades from Dosin Pali arrive in the harbor
Baria Setral, his brother Mesker Setral, Orto (commander of Aren Company)
Forty Red Blades prepare to attack the people in the market
Ten Wickans, planted by Coltaine in the market, emerge from the panic and face the Red Blades
Kulp readies his warrens & warns against the Red Blades
The Hissar Guard and Wickan bowmen arrive to outnumber and escort the expected arrival of the Red Blades to Fist Coltaine
The Red Blades sheath their weapons and concede

Kulp informs that Coltaine ordered sappers to transform a ruined monastery on a hill south of Hissar into a training ground for war games involving mock battles, street control, assaulting buildings, break out tactics, retrieving wounded, etc.
Every afternoon the Wickans work the 7th army until night to exhaustion
Each soldier died a dozen times in the war games, Corporal List died in every one
Coltaine has Kulp conjure illusions simulating chaotic, humorously uncooperative Malazan refugees
Sormo E’nath whereabouts is unknown while Coltaine is for some reason already preparing his army into being guardians of Malazan refugees
Duiker encourages Kulp to keep at it and he might talk Coltaine into a day of rest
Corporal List “dies” in the first few minutes of a mock engagement
Bult goes to retrieve him
The 7th Army is improving, more Wickan victims than the 7th Army
The 7th Army turned the tide when encouraged by a day of rest
Coltaine gives the 7th the support of his lancers to finish off the war games, rewards their day off, and is proud
Fiddler and Crokus argue about how Kalam left them to deliver the Book to Sha’ik
“Another crack in Lasseen’s crumbling control”
Kalam will take the mundane, overland and ship route to Unta
Fiddler and crew will take another path that might not work
Apsalar is moody
Crokus accuses that if Kalam fails, Fiddler will try to prod the Rope’s assassin skills from Apsalar and use her to kill Laseen
Fiddler realizes that Kalam and QB considered exactly that
Fiddler tells Crokus to stop white knighting for her
Moby appears and Crokus learns he’s a bhok’aral, a species native to Seven Cities, and that despite being Uncle Mammot’s familiar he still remains after Mammot died
Fiddler, Crokus, and Apsalar prepare to leave
They notice since Ehrlitan’s paranoid Fist had withdrawn the garrison troops there’s little to no Malazan patrols
Disguised as a Gral escorting newlywed pilgrims to visit all seven Holy Cities, brings five horses and four mules
Red Blades appear and one stops Fiddler at the gate to ask about a lone rider (Kalam)
Fiddler intends to reach G’danisban in a week, Kalam being 2-3 days ahead
Wary of the convergence of shapeshifters in the Pan’potsun Odhan past G’danisban
The Spiritwalker’s conch shell may attract them, plan to sell it in G’danisban
Moby flew off and disappeared, Fiddler and Crokus bond over Mammot’s death
Apsalar is still moody
Iskaral Pust is cleaning the chimney and tells Mappo to kill any spiders he sees
Mappo fever caused by the D’ivers leopard bite on his neck had broken
Soletaken/D’ivers bites appear to be venomous causing illness, hallucinations, bestial madness, then death. Survivors have recurrent episodes each year
Mappo would rather suicide than live with the venom that would make him go berserk
Mappo goes to find Icarium in the temple library
Mappo finds Icarium in the library, which also doubles as a kitchen where Servant is boiling linens in the cauldron
Icarium is astonished by the books Iskaral possesses
Books thousands of years old, composed of ludicrously expensive materials for such “pointless, trite subjects” in languages long dead, yet Icarium can comprehend
Looking at the ancient script, Mappo recalls a memory of escorting his tribe’s elders to perform a ritual, using rune-etched staves, which determined Mappo’s future
Icarium sees a symbol of a twisted staff on the spine
He believes the books support his belief that a thriving civilization had existed on Seven Cities, possibly the first human civilization which all others come from
Icarium is obsessed with time, even making mechanisms to measure time (primitive clocks)
Mappo grows uncomfortable and expresses his suspicion that Shadow had expected their arrival at this temple and Iskaral has plans involving them
Motivation: Icarium feels the temple will lead him to his goal (of chasing time and regaining his memories)
As Icarium asks for his patience, Mappo further recalls the memory of his elder’s summoning ritual
The elders called upon a human face belonging to the Nameless Ones
The Nameless One addresses Mappo as Chosen Warrior and asks “What can you learn of patience?”
Mappo references Gothos’ Folly to argue that seeking knowledge poisons the mind
Mappo watches Servant wringing the boiling water from the linens and notices one arm looking unweathered and youthful, the other arm more fitting of his age in muscles and tanned skin
Servant does not respond to Mappo’s attempt at conversation
The duo leave to explore the rest of the temple
Tesem Temple (approximation)
Skullcup (approximation)
A mine tunnel collapsed, where Heboric had worked before Felisin pushed his transfer, killing everyone inside
Two weeks since Heboric was transferred from pushing carts to tilling Deepsoil
His health improved thanks to Felisin’s arrangements, but their relationship remains strained
Felisin becomes more addicted to the durhang opiate, more numb, increasingly seeking to be used by Beneth and his friends
Pella, the gate guard, finds Felisin, sees that she's damaged by the durhang use, and asks for Heboric
Meta: Can guess at this point Pella is Duiker and Kulp’s inside man
Beneth takes Felisin to Capt. Sawark, informs him that four mages had died in the tunnel collapse but not the one he sought
Beneth asks why Baudin, who was his strong asset, was arrested and learns Baudin broke curfew and ran away but got caught
Offers Felisin as a gift to Sawark in exchange for someone to replace Baudin, was rejected
Beneth vents his rage on Felisin beating her
Asks who Baudin is and who she is
Felisin lies and claims to have been a priestess in training for Fener
Felisin was left passed out in the street until Heboric found her and took her home nursing her
Heboric had spare time after finishing his work, heard Baudin had escaped jail and is at large, and asked Beneth where Felisin is and spends the night looking for her
Felisin wants Beneth to take her back
Kalam heads towards Ladro Keep, south of Ehrlitan, by horse
Avoids a cloud of chigger fleas
Endures through a storm and reaches the Keep
Kalam enters the Ladro Keep gatehouse
Inside sit a few Malazan soldiers and a merchant with his wife
Kalam shows the Sergeant his Clawmaster symbol in private
A Pardu woman (Lostara Yil) and an Ehrlii man storm in, bitten by chigger fleas
To avoid conflict the Pardu woman buys drinks for everyone
Kalam rejects the merchant’s wife proposal to read his fortune using the Deck of Dragons
Kalam calls her out as a scam and she throws the Deck at him
On the floor was the Rope, Assassin of Shadow
Surrounded by High House Death: King, Herald, Mason, Spinner, Knight, and Queen
Kalam leaves Ladro Keep
Red Blade Captain Lostara Yil and her companion kills everyone in Ladro Keep and continue following Kalam
Mappo and Icarium descend into a crypt they believed was made by the nuns of the Life-aspected Queen of Dreams before they left
